newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - C&W welcomes Chinese commitment to HK Telecom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - C&W welcomes Chinese commitment to HK Telecom.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc on Friday welcomed Chinese investment in its Hongkong Telecom subsidiary as the end of British rule in the colony loomed.
"We welcome the proposed investment by China Everbright in Hongkong Telecom," said Brian Smith, chairman of British-based telecommunications giant C&W.
"This substantial investment of Chinese state capital demonstrates continued confidence in Hongkong Telecom and Hong Kong through the 1997 transition and beyond," he added.
C&W shares added 10.5p to 512p as the London market reacted positively to the news, which came just a few weeks before the colony is handed over to China.

However, share analysts in Hong Kong described the planned deal as an "anticlimax". They noted that China Everbright was buying a 7.74 percent stake from a company which is also ultimately controlled by the Chinese state.

C&W owns almost 60 percent of Hongkong Telecom and there has been speculation about its plans as Britain prepares to bring down the curtain on more than 150 years of rule. The territory will be handed over to China on July 1.
London-based analysts said C&W may cut its stake in Hongkong Telecom to 51 percent in return for access to the Chinese market but would not want to cede control.
"They've always said it's a fundamental plank in their portfolio," said Richard Jones of brokers Yamaichi.
Hongkong Telecom accounted for 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion) of a total Cable & Wireless turnover of 5.5 billion pounds in 1995/96.

C&W chief executive Dick Brown this week declined comment on the Hongkong unit's strategic plans. But it is thought likely to seek a partner in China where foreign companies may not participate directly in the telecoms market.
Analysts said Friday's planned deal was the not the "big bang" move the market had been anticipating.
China Everbright has agreed in principle to buy the stake in Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd for HK$11.4 billion ($1.47 billion).
Both China Everbright and CITIC Pacific's ultimate parent are controlled by China's State Council. C&W officials noted that the link was more direct in the case of China Everbright.
